correctness.rationale: A forward-invariant biological simplex, exact \(x_1/S\) monotonicity, and a bipartite product bound give uniform leading-species persistence. The exact derivative of \(\log(x_i/x_1)\) makes even coordinates exponentially small and odd ratios converge positively by induction. A logistic total-density equation with exponentially decaying predation forces convergence to the carrying mass. Integrable deviations of odd limiting densities yield exact positive extinction prefactors. Standalone code verified 540 finite-time identities and 20 long-time assertions; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: The motivating ecological question is which of many equilibrium supports is dynamically selected. The source independent-set count and local stability do not answer universal full-interior selection. The result proves that one alternating community is globally selected for every strictly positive initial state at arbitrary chain length and quantifies the exact late-time extinction of all excluded levels, including positive leading amplitudes, making the assertion predictive for finite-time persistence scales.
